thesis: SEZL is a beta-6.6 consumer-credit name being bought into a confirmed risk-off tape (QQQ below 50/200-day, VIX 1y percentile 0.905, yields at a 0.90 percentile), where high-beta growth is the first thing sold. The post-earnings gap to 178.55 was sold into on 1.97M volume, the 11-16 spike to 167.95 was rejected, and 11-17 closed down 4.7%, so the good news is already priced and distribution is visible. Retail euphoria (Zacks Bull of the Day, IBD coverage) arriving right at a failed rally is a classic late-crowd signal, and short interest of 23.1% of float cuts both ways: a squeeze needs a catalyst, and none is scheduled before Feb-Mar 2027. BNPL peers are weak (Affirm down on 11-18, Chime IPO looming), and an unexplained DEFA14A and an 8-K 7.01 are unchecked. The 154 entry sits only a few points above the 144.5 stop, and a gap through it in this tape is plausible.
